prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: There’s no single universally “best” HVAC company for everyone in Atlanta — the best one for you depends on your ZIP code, budget, timeline, the size/age of your home, and whether you want a national chain or a local contractor. If you give me your ZIP code (or neighborhood) I can pull up top-rated installers near you and compare them.  

While you decide, here are practical steps and what to look for so you pick the right company for an AC replacement:

What I need from you to give specific recommendations
- ZIP code or neighborhood
- Home type (single-family, townhouse, condo)
- Approximate square footage or number of bedrooms
- Rough budget or brand preference (Trane, Carrier, Lennox, Goodman, etc.)
- Any timeline constraints (need it done ASAP?)
- Are you replacing the full system (air handler + condensing unit + ductwork) or just the outdoor unit?

How to pick the best company (quick checklist)
- License and insurance: Ask to see state/local HVAC license and proof of insurance.
- NATE-certified technicians: indicates trained techs.
- Experience and local references: years in business and recent local references.
- Written quote and scope: includes equipment model numbers, SEER rating, labor, permit fees, and removal of old unit.
- Proper sizing: insist on a Manual J load calculation and, if needed, duct evaluation (not just “rule of thumb” sizing).
- Installation quality: ask about coil accessibility, condenser pad, line-set length/insulation, proper refrigerant charge, and startup paperwork.
- Warranties: equipment manufacturer warranty and installer (labor) warranty.
- Permits and inspections: contractor should pull permits and arrange final inspection if required.
- Financing and rebates: availability of financing, utility rebates, or tax credits.
- Good reviews and BBB/Angi/HomeAdvisor ratings; avoid companies with repeated pattern of complaints.

Questions to ask every contractor (bring this to appointments)
1. Are you licensed and insured? Can I see proof?
2. Will you perform a Manual J load calculation and provide it in writing?
3. What brand and model do you recommend and why? What is the SEER rating?
4. What exactly is included in the price (permit, startup, removal, line set, thermostat)?
5. What warranties do you offer on equipment and labor?
6. Who will perform the work — company employees or subcontractors?
7. Do you include a refrigerant charge and check for correct superheat/subcooling?
8. How long will the installation take and when can you start?
9. Can you provide recent local references or examples of similar installs?
10. Do you offer financing or know about local rebates?

Ballpark cost (Atlanta area, approximate)
- Small replacement (just condensing unit, no ductwork): often $3,000–6,000 depending on tonnage and SEER.
- Full system replacement (air handler + condenser ± ducts): often $5,000–12,000 or more depending on home size, brand, and duct changes.
(These are rough ranges; get written quotes.)

If you want, I can:
- Look up top-rated HVAC companies near you (give ZIP)
- Compare 3–5 companies on licensing, reviews, years in business, and typical warranties
- Produce a short list of questions tailored to each company’s estimate

Which would you like me to do next?
